name: Deb Haaland
subject: Can I tell you a bit about my story?
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | |
---
Hey, friend — it’s Deb. Can I tell you a bit about my story?

From my great-grandmother, mother, and many before them, I’m blessed to come from generations of Pueblo women who taught me what it means to be fierce and resilient.
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=1&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-)
Some of my earliest memories are of watching my grandmother bake bread in her mud oven and stir huge pots of [**posole**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=2&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-). I’d perch myself outside and watch her through the window for hours. To this day, there’s nothing I enjoy more than making traditional New Mexican meals for my friends and family.
For me, cooking has always been a way to foster connection and build community, which is exactly what we’re doing now in this campaign. I’ve had the chance to sit down with New Mexicans in living rooms, at kitchen tables, in restaurants, parks — in all 33 counties — to hear about their lives, their struggles, and their hopes for the future. Those conversations are a reminder of just how high the stakes are in this race and why I’m in it: **to fight for and deliver for New Mexicans.**
Friend, more and more, we are seeing extremism take place and a President who isn’t fighting for us. Democratic Governors — including this seat right here in New Mexico — are essential to serve as a backstop when the federal government abuses its resources and undermines civil liberties.
As Governor, I will fight to expand healthcare access, lower costs, build stronger schools, and invest in safer communities. Meanwhile, the Republicans in this race want to open New Mexico to Trump’s extremist agenda. **That’s why this race is so important.**
Fox News is calling New Mexico a top flip opportunity for Republicans. Now more than ever, the support of every single member of this team matters.
I feel so grateful for this grassroots community — including you, friend. [**Since you're a member of our team, I’d like to share my favorite New Mexican recipe, green chile chicken posole, with you today.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=3&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-)**** This recipe means a lot to my family, and I hope that you’ll enjoy it with your family, too.
| | [VIEW RECIPE >>>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12133?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&code=jtk911-su-nd&t=4&akid=10404%2E400544%2EDV1uB-)
---
Friend, thank you for letting me take a moment of your time to share my story and why this campaign means so much to me. We’ve got a lot of work ahead, so fuel up with a pot of posole and get ready! With good food and good friends, we can do anything.
Be Fierce,
Deb
|

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: I can’t stop thinking about this...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
Peter, I know it’s late, but I can’t stop thinking about these AIPAC ads.
In case you missed it, AIPAC-aligned groups have unleashed **_$16 million_** worth of ads to try and prop up their preferred candidate.
I know. It’s a lot to wrap your head around. But can I be brutally honest with you, Peter?
**I think we can still win.**
AIPAC has done this before in primary races like this one. They've spent millions to target campaigns who wouldn’t play by their rules, and most of those races, one of these two scenarios plays out:
1. When a campaign has the resources to tell its own story, AIPAC's ads don't stick the way they're supposed to.
2. When a campaign runs dry and can't respond — that's when AIPAC’s ads seal their fate.

So the honest answer to whether we get through this isn't complicated. **It comes down to whether we have enough grassroots power to run our own ads, reach voters, and control our own narrative before AIPAC controls it for us.**
I wouldn't be writing to you if I didn't believe that what you do tonight matters to what happens in this race. Peter, if you can pitch in $5 or anything to fuel our campaign, it would make a huge impact. Can I count on your support?

Democrats ALREADY redrew the maps in California to steal Conservative seats, they're ALREADY investing half a billion to swamp the airwaves with Liberal propaganda, and they're ALREADY outperforming us in key special elections.
If we don't get serious now, Election Day 2026 will be doomsday for MAGA.
So here's what it all boils down to. If we lose the House:

* President Trump will be impeached. In fact, that's what's driving their Liberal donors to give again and again

name: Thompson 4ND
subject: Re: We wont take this attack sitting down!
body:
Dear Friend,

Rob Port has a lot to say about what we as Democrats believe. Yesterday, he
made another miscalculation
<https://www.inforum.com/opinion/columns/port-democrats-set-to-repeat-their-oil-boom-blunder>:
that Democrats are on the wrong side of the data center issue, and we were
too alarmist about the Oil Boom.

The AI Data Center land rush is not the same as the Oil Boom. One creates
energy, the other takes it away.

If you agree that data centers need more oversight, join our movement..
<https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>

[image: image.png] <https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>

I’ve been in the oil patch for 15 years. Data centers are not the Bakken
oil field. The Bakken was studied before industry came to town. Where have
the data center studies been? What will be the long-term impact 15 or even
50 years from now? And why in the world are public officials signing NDAs
for data center projects? If you want those same answers, join us
<https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>.

I seem to be the only candidate talking to concerned citizens and doing
research on this. You can see my work here
<https://www.thompson4nd.com/data-center-resources>.

[image: image.png] <https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>

We aren’t going to take this sitting down. I am going on Rob Port’s Plain
Talk podcast on Wednesday to discuss responsible data center development.

There are 27 existing and proposed data centers across ND. Chip in $27
today to help us force the multi-billion dollar out-of-state corporations
to be more transparent. <https://www.thompson4nd.com/donate>

Thank you for your time.

Sincerely,

Vern Thompson
Candidate for ND Agriculture Commissioner
thompson4nd@gmail.com
701-400-6767
thompson4nd.com

Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | | • | Behind the Markets ---|--- | • | Weiss Ratings Plus ---|--- | • | Salem Media Group ---|--- | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ## US-Iran Talks Resume in Switzerland
U.S. and Iran are set to [resume nuclear negotiations](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ8GOiOzgCGFi7-hy99eiRZ7nTi32JFtwuXtT-QVrhyNNJrv-7ouV_Tsw-0_bqSLi0ugIzOVQmkpyN85Ud43aqXEYHPxzBbDAhKUkEpAu1j0_F762mpHBNTVpNtxAtmpfhjqu55wtW5aW6ecnVaUqjMjmEl2l2nA1dna63NNKmhbKccOGmVIAfUrqvGCREPVS7K-xNQ8og_lTo7f8UWpMXGrWd9Leeaq-1fBXMF8HEfj4s9JcfYVzOxfJM5cwbxn4RMG8SQ0JCwhi7AbJkziAyt8TkgsmFYMMQgTg2NvinjsgQTIOmn7PDyzz2qsennb0PPnR_mTvJeG3wAAAP__oYeFaQ) in Switzerland this weekend, with envoy Steve Witkoff and adviser Jared Kushner leading the delegation. The talks restart a day after a brief postponement. The reset followed a fresh Israel-Hezbollah truce, [brokered Friday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGSrCAYhE-DmRb8KGpA8BKzeemGFkqrzCBOATPW7Om33Cts3vV19_d1G2_GeRfW_2aHzssxBpzJI2fEMRv_SBHptUNwboJN2XlvTRiJkyq5KkmM1jj_GevC6gUgyAJatB1xqeqmKTZNHUcnSYqmX_jUSj5Z4u3UE286KexcOH3RuCIhOG8lVWqGItSTUW1vgIbVHNblI1b3w4W8YfGf441YzcdeeL3l_ExM_mM0MBrO86xOkzYX1nyE7HakK8douI4xGq4yRsP9FRgNomc0uBQNfLnhezq8N1tp1giUEQEnbDnDJCwuokw5ugcuSBG1fZ7Oe5dUy2q-7sb53z35TxLfmn4CAAD__zRMhUY) by the U.S. and Qatar through talks with Israel and Iran. It took effect at 4 p.m. local time after Israeli strikes killed at least 18 people in southern Lebanon. A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah appeared increasingly fragile as Israel refused to withdraw from a buffer zone and Hezbollah launched about 50 projectiles, prompting fresh Israeli strikes. The 14-point memorandum signed on Wednesday gives negotiators a 60-day deadline. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected on Sunday, as Vice President JD Vance says [oil is again flowing](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMR2RGRtDChe3octtt0QTPITZHewIJomyT79iX2HrX_qkcz4u4wVZON_-40pR5zJmeu1CqrSNivK1b7Q_VmqsxZx2ZZGEeQQLobahhmZMyPIefZXiTATkKopN14N1wbdttUSfoHeug2lOwaFNHcxI5NtzR9h7vFYcD80GaBprOwenMFEA8lcM3RmJWuMtJdaynT4LZ11olnd50naaylpJXFTvu3H_DAwGBl1oYZGjGRiWstIxyMCAaeXMu26oXLKBoT07CH1bPzFPVB-BtV7Ktj6-68JSz1JeBoZqi-n-YhHeQ2e8va3Iv3ylf_rrGeEnAAD__-Y_fyU) through the Strait of Hormuz near prewar levels.
## Judge Delays Release of Biden Tapes
A federal judge has [blocked the release](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdEZmAZMULq6hy7VXIsdew-aMHdmboLz9L_IKfzfSfBrNzL_bcrMUKa1_7Y6GQ14SHjUiM5aFbfxfC9bXjp1SNvnKFKO3aQEFWiotoVu8pfhZhsabgAjYN2i66QKq18M4NptR1-4yjsPYq9ANOoxX5Z0LFxfATv2JkDnTlIauU2rqodUONeBwt3q6WsRRDAo9cS7tI1PiDUP85DeW1uW9iWZjflbR_xEwC5iP42jdvZ4rTl_AfEoB8508Jvl4VSaH0uPTFt4xsXQ5VSxvy5RTleuWKx-FGIvcsBDbFWXIr-S_gIC5KcY_D4qRqp7EoNbdUvx24V8d-DbwEwAA__8DhYcb) of audio and transcripts from former President Joe Biden's interviews with the ghostwriter of his 2017 memoir, ordering a three-week pause for an appeals court to weigh in. The Trump-appointed judge acted hours after [first clearing the records](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO3CAYhJ8Gd6zgXxuvC4o0dHdNEqW0wMx62cNgAXvWvn3kvEKaaUaa-fT9-Zg_bIghrZ92g273PCccNaI1lLnZ-FUL6muDFMImX1uI0ds0kyDFheIkZ29DfM995_UdIFw7aDneSFxVPwzdQ0s5SGWlo-nmHADRww0TWdc7S0SuC_pcE4qkFGK80kUtUITeWTVOFhhYL-BDy-XyzCG1B-7xnb9RLkveuqgfre2VXX8wMozMcRyX1x7OjpH5lff5E0dlZH7_ZGTOJ0ZGnCEnRub58iu4i3n5qvz5qi0s4B67LW1DarwgwlZwFzwSdyGvxe4PFF6w5OJDWhmZSSg53uQk6SYkI9MV7fcjxBiqGlkv1s2G-I-2_Zfib01_AwAA__-6mI1V). The files stem from special counsel Robert Hur's classified-documents probe, which ended without charges but flagged Biden's faltering memory. A conservative think tank has [pressed a FOIA lawsuit](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLEO2yAUAL8Gb1jwwNgeGLp4S9eOFjGPmARDBM-x8vdV20_ofjqd7tdtvbmYYn78dAdaCmXNeLWERFhXcunVKrbzQCmEy75RTMm7vIIAw4XhIFfvYvquuvM2IAKqDq0cJxDK6GHodqulhkkNKuhtDLN006jCfZNeeD3DFLCL9o9NGJBSiFFBbzY0gPruzDg7xIFpgT5Sqf2zxEw7hvQtH6z9Vo4u2Z3o3Zj6wWBhsFzX1W_lrJRiI8z_KAaLL9sLicFiJiXNNM4Mlh1rJPdAHsqZvaNYMv_ws3GPb1fpwEy8BP48G8UNGSxdtf59xZRiMyPT4nG4mP5m0H-9-1j4HQAA__9wOYMG) for two years, after the Justice Department reversed course and agreed to release redacted versions. The D.C. Circuit will decide whether to extend the block. Biden, now a private citizen, calls the decade-old conversations private.
## Father's Day Spending Hits New High
The Father's Day gift has come a long way from the pipes and neckties of generations past, and this year shoppers are pouring a [record $27.9 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb0T4GUMZGLp4S9eO1rN5jmkxWPCaKH9fpb_Q7eoOR0fn8zpfMaaYbx94kOetzJkeLREz1ZkxfbdK7eegXinMoXFMKWCeQYGRykjo54AxPWfdBb8RAQ0d-d6-gRqMHsdu9y5op7fBBbfYcbTj0js9DC5gIAP9il30L5oy0PdK2QEuZiUDpBc01iHRKLSiELnUy1eJmXfa0rPcqV7WcnTJ78xnE8O7gEnAlOv2-gVMB4WIcqXMVAVMZ6XWZKVE2KgJmDbknapsMuBTtpNyiPkmucg9sqy0lhokWOnkElOKJXfVh_Px2s1YodXtwJj-HPhf4e4efgMAAP__CWKCJA) into dad, up from $24 billion in 2025. Tastes have [shifted over the decades](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHOozAQRk8DHZE9gFkKF9vQZdst0YDH4GSwI3tIxO1X2Sv87adP70nv732-Y-AQtz94kBWf5kifwiRCeRbkZ8lUzoO0UhhdkcDsMM6gwDTKNKBnh4Gvuaud9URAbU1WD79Atabr-3q3hNgtxpvB6NFpGtHAiuvS99qPqiesg_3SlAGtlRpauJmVDFC3oBlGJOqrTpELkvLtkUKUnTxf6U35tqajZruLvErV_q5gqmBaTu-R0wPXZ0nxe_mOnLZSwfRIZ47IFUweZadcGodXswUvjWSKrjSy53Rue7OHIilfdbbu9QnMoZih6tR2YOD_XvlRrLeFfwEAAP__beKAFQ), from tobacco and grooming kits toward clothing, electronics, and experiences, but the classics endure: [greeting cards and clothing](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOpCAUBeCnwQ6DV8SxoNjGbrbd0lzhMjKDYIAd49tv3Ff46y85Oef8eS5P9MHH12_cSVeXlkhnCVQr5aVi-JRM5e9OnRAYbak-BItxAQGKC8WhWyz6cC2ysdoRAfUN6W58gOiVHIZm0wYezplpIhqlEbLrJdqhQyPRDYLWtfH6ThMKuk6IsYdWGVJAckU1Tkg0MCnI-ppy-04-1o1cuNKXcmvS3gS91XoU1v9iMDOYz_NszVruFbczmCOdV8ofBvPXW0oMZtwpe4Ox8COnN5lKltfEy0HRchj5xFcfgk-Rp8gd1o1y4RYvBnOTtT3OW4samRSvHX34X6T-6L2vhn8BAAD__7zWhO8) top the list at 60% and 58%, ahead of a special outing and gift cards. The average shopper now plans to spend $226.58, a record, with budgets rising across nearly every age group.

**Whatever happened to the metal lunch box?** For about 35 years, the most contested real estate in American pop culture measured roughly 8 inches by 7 inches: the side of a steel lunch box. From 1950 to 1985, whoever ruled the airwaves ruled the cafeteria, until plastic, economics, and worried parents brought the era clanging to a close. The lunch box began as strictly blue-collar gear, a plain metal container for the working man. The revolution came in 1950, when Aladdin Industries stamped [TV cowboy Hopalong Cassidy on a steel box](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVvQcRgTBg9d2NK1IzrsI1xq7Mh2EuXtq_YV-gL_L31fl-VCEiReP-lgW7e0RH6VwLVyXiqF75K5PA7uACj6UiUET3FBQHMCc8Ju8SThvejG240ZuW_YduMZoTd6GJrdgps8wwTE27R2ACudQROaVWvc-gEasb81MNh1AGOPrXFskPVKZpyIeVAa2EtNub0liXXnLbzTk3Pr0tEEu9d6L6r_UDgrnOngLI7iLqWm_G6LtOwfCmeXQmBXJcWicE7rjV1VOMeD9qXDAeAMTbb-_pIQpJhRabgeJOHvUv9F87T4EwAA__9etXcO), the first lunch box to bear a licensed image. Sales jumped from 50,000 units to 600,000 in a single year. Rival American Thermos fired back in 1953 with a full-color lithographed Roy Rogers box, and the arms race was on. Carrying last year's box was social suicide, which, of course, was the key to the whole business model. It was the Golden Age of illustrated metal lunch boxes. By the late 1970s, though, the steel box had a target on its back. Schoolyard legend holds that mothers' groups, alarmed by kids swinging their boxes like medieval maces, lobbied to have metal lunch boxes banned as weapons, starting, the story goes, with Florida. It was a perfect tale: the lunch box as both treasure and cudgel. It's also, apparently, a myth. No such Florida law was ever passed. The truth was duller and more decisive: plastic was simply cheaper, and by the early 1980s, the accountants had won the fight. Over 1,000,000 men already use it. - | Whatever happened to the metal lunch box? For about 35 years, the most contested real estate in American pop culture measured roughly 8 inches by 7 inches: the side of a steel lunch box. From 1950 to 1985, whoever ruled the airwaves ruled the cafeteria, until plastic, economics, and worried parents brought the era clanging to a close. The lunch box began as strictly blue-collar gear, a plain metal container for the working man. The revolution came in 1950, when Aladdin Industries stamped , the first lunch box to bear a licensed image. Sales jumped from 50,000 units to 600,000 in a single year. Rival American Thermos fired back in 1953 with a full-color lithographed Roy Rogers box, and the arms race was on. For three decades, the lunch box served as a kid's first public declaration of identity: Davy Crockett or Zorro, or the Monkees, Star Trek or . Carrying last year's box was social suicide, which, of course, was the key to the whole business model. It was the Golden Age of illustrated metal lunch boxes. By the late 1970s, though, the steel box had a target on its back. Schoolyard legend holds that mothers' groups, alarmed by kids swinging their boxes like medieval maces, lobbied to have metal lunch boxes banned as weapons, starting, the story goes, with Florida. It was a perfect tale: the lunch box as both treasure and cudgel. It's also, apparently, a myth. No such Florida law was ever passed. The truth was duller and more decisive: plastic was simply cheaper, and by the early 1980s, the accountants had won the fight. The end came in 1985 with marking the final metal lunch box produced before safety worries and economics finished the switch to plastic. Soft-sided nylon followed, and the steel pop-culture-branded lunch box retired to the collectibles market, where the very boxes Mom tossed out now fetch hundreds, sometimes thousands, at auction. Imagine growing up in a country where owning a Bible is illegal.

| | | | | [](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkcGOmzAQhp_G3ED2mHXCgUOVlFPTqlWl3RtyxgO4i21km0X79pWj5gF6_b_5fmlmXm_jTdvV-vm7dtTHPI0xjXmhT9SOcjh0xiUFRIolHIGDqrmqQZQ5UZneoNECK-rF6QxcdkqKauk7Op2h1RpbYfA-0b09Kymntj13ShGIyvaliisQQnAOqnkRctL8pZPCAJHRrOV6pZibSNt-Xy1qn3V6n0JEajC4au2XnLfE5BcGA4PhOI7GunsT4sxgmMlTDMnmz4JCXE2N-1aDqvOi_XsqjhwSzY58vgRDTF5fL6AYqC2GP4SP8McHxWgf8Nvt0r29cQ4gOgZqz25E7TZtZ8_k9cDx4ZY4hT1iUbYY0kaYrZ__IUfG7o7JKzlt12dN8Jl8ZvL69Qbjz1P96_dQP69Txd5sh11Xm9SJtXwu4mP__P_f-ujhbwAAAP__3SSjGg)

Dear Friend,

Imagine growing up in a country where owning a Bible is illegal.

Where the name of Jesus is not spoken in public. Where choosing to follow Christ could cost you your family, your job, or your freedom. Where a missionary can’t get a visa.

For millions of people, this is not a hypothetical. It is everyday life.

This summer, many of them are coming to the World Cup.

They are coming to cheer for their national team and experience something larger than themselves. When they arrive in cities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, they will step into something they never experienced before — a place where someone can walk up to them, hand them a Gospel of John in their language, and tell them about Jesus without anyone stopping it.

_This moment is what we are preparing for._

IMB teams will be on the ground in Fan Zones and near stadiums throughout the tournament. Trained volunteers will be ready to have conversations, distribute resources, and connect fans with digital discipleship tools in their language that they can take home — back to countries where that kind of follow-up would otherwise be impossible.

For some of these fans, this will be the only time in their lives they are handed the gospel freely.

We cannot show up unprepared.

You can help us be ready by giving a gift today.

Here is what your gift does:

* $25 — 200 evangelism tracts placed directly into the hands of fans
* $50 — 25 soccer patches for sparking evangelistic conversations
* $100 — 100 Gospel of John booklets
* $250 — Rents an English Club outreach location where fans can hear the gospel in a welcoming space

At the Paris Olympics and the Winter Olympics, this approach worked. Thousands of spiritual conversations occurred. Tens of thousands of New Testaments were distributed. People made commitments to Christ during conversations with our teams. People interested in the gospel connected with discipleship tools that followed them home to their own countries.

The World Cup is far-reaching. The opportunity to connect with people who have never had access to hear the gospel is greater than anything we have seen at a single event.

But only if we are there, fully funded and fully prepared.

**Will you give today to ensure our teams are on the ground and ready for the World Cup?**

[Click here to give. ](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyUkcGOmzAQhp_G3ED2mHXCgUOVlFPTqlWl3RtyxgO4i21km0X79pWj5gF6_b_5fmlmXm_jTdvV-vm7dtTHPI0xjXmhT9SOcjh0xiUFRIolHIGDqrmqQZQ5UZneoNECK-rF6QxcdkqKauk7Op2h1RpbYfA-0b09Kymntj13ShGIyvaliisQQnAOqnkRctL8pZPCAJHRrOV6pZibSNt-Xy1qn3V6n0JEajC4au2XnLfE5BcGA4PhOI7GunsT4sxgmMlTDMnmz4JCXE2N-1aDqvOi_XsqjhwSzY58vgRDTF5fL6AYqC2GP4SP8McHxWgf8Nvt0r29cQ4gOgZqz25E7TZtZ8_k9cDx4ZY4hT1iUbYY0kaYrZ__IUfG7o7JKzlt12dN8Jl8ZvL69Qbjz1P96_dQP69Txd5sh11Xm9SJtXwu4mP__P_f-ujhbwAAAP__3SSjGg)
